case: The same eight boundary kinds in a different order, which must not be refused.
why: The control keys on MEMBERSHIP. An enum's members are a set, `in` does not read order, and no predicate in the registry does either -- so a byte comparison would refuse a reordering that changes no admissible transfer, and a control that refuses harmless edits is one contributors learn to route around. This is the same argument r20 makes for the custody tie-break enum, and it is made again here rather than assumed to carry, because the assertion is a different literal in a different place.
